title: Forgiveness
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Forgiving never means a child must stay in danger: always add "and tell a trusted adult".

skills.key_step: The child says why we forgive (God forgives us; it brings peace), that Matthew 5:39 teaches not to repay evil with evil, and that forgiving means letting go of revenge, not pretending, and still telling an adult when unsafe.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the story of the unforgiving servant.
floor.question: What did the unforgiving servant refuse to do?

representations: two hands: one tight fist (revenge), one open (forgive)
a story card of a playground quarrel
steps: Do not pay back evil with evil.
Let go of the wish to get even.
If it is unsafe, tell an adult.
contexts: a classmate who spoils your drawing
a brother who takes your toy

board.do: Draw a tight fist and an open hand.

board.say: What does revenge do? What does the verse ask instead?

board.do: Wait for the child to say do not pay back.
Write Matthew 5:39 under the open hand.

misconceptions.ask: Someone hits you. According to Matthew 5:39, what should you do?
misconceptions.repair: Role-play walking away and telling the teacher.

misconceptions.ask: Is forgiving a sign of weakness?
misconceptions.repair: Say that forgiving is a choice and that telling a teacher keeps you safe.

misconceptions.ask: What does it mean to forgive someone?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what changes in us when we stop planning revenge.

listen_for: Stand still and let him keep hitting
misconceptions.ask: What does "turn the other cheek" (Matthew 5:39) ask a child to do when hit by a bully?
misconceptions.repair: Explain: the verse is about not paying back. A child still goes to a safe place and tells a teacher.

checks.question: Someone hits you. What does Matthew 5:39 teach?
checks.answer: Do not pay back evil with evil

checks.question: Does forgiving mean pretending it never happened?
checks.answer: No: it means letting go of revenge
